newsitem.title: USA: NY Gov's welfare plan would cut benefits - papers.
newsitem.headline: NY Gov's welfare plan would cut benefits - papers.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki's new plan for welfare reforms includes a measure to gradually cut monthly benefits for families but let them keep more of any funds they earn, newspapers reported Tuesday.
New York Times and Albany Times Union, in their Tuesday editions, said the Republican governor is expected to propose his new plan Wednesday.

The program, which is expected to face stiff opposition in the Democrat-led Assembly, would reduce a family's benefit by 10 percent after being on the program for 18 months. A 45-percent reduction would apply if a family collected benefits for four years, the papers said. And after five years, the benefits would end.
Slashing welfare benefits is expected to free up money that can be used to close looming budget gaps, like the one for the 1998 fiscal year, which is estimated at $3 billion.
A proposal to let families keep up to $1,080 a month from jobs without having their benefits reduced would help offset the proposed cuts, New York Times said.
And the state would spend an additional $130 million for a total of $630 million for child care and employment programs, the papers said.
